macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Global shares mixed as U.S. futures rebound and oil drops
items.summary: Global equities were mixed Monday, while U.S. stock futures rose after Wall Street’s sharp Friday selloff. Oil prices fell nearly 4% amid renewed hopes for diplomatic progress between the U.S. and Iran.[3]

items.title: Technology selloff drives steep Friday losses
items.summary: The S&P 500 fell 1.8% Friday, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.9%, and the Dow declined 1.1% as investors sold technology and artificial-intelligence stocks amid concerns that AI spending may have become excessive.[3]

items.title: U.S. futures rise ahead of earnings and midterm elections
items.summary: Premarket trading showed the Nasdaq up about 0.8%, with the S&P 500 and Dow each gaining roughly 0.5%. Investors were preparing for Apple and Palantir earnings Monday, AMD results Tuesday, U.S. midterm elections, and a major week of economic data.[4]

items.title: Fed holds rates steady as markets assess possible future hikes
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept the federal funds target range at 3.75%-4.00% in a 10-2 decision, with two dissenting officials preferring a 25-basis-point increase. Investors are awaiting Fed speakers and labor-market data for clues about the next policy move.[2]

items.title: Fed considers fewer policy meetings
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is considering a schedule with fewer rate-setting meetings next year, a change that could make each policy decision more consequential for financial markets.[1]

items.title: Major economic data and central-bank decisions ahead
items.summary: This week’s calendar includes U.S. payrolls, JOLTS, ADP employment, ISM surveys, Fed speeches, and policy decisions from the Reserve Bank of Australia and Bank of England. Markets were pricing expectations for rate increases from both foreign central banks.[2]

items.title: Apple, Palantir and AMD headline earnings slate
items.summary: Apple and Palantir were scheduled to report after Monday’s close, followed by AMD on Tuesday. The results are expected to test investor confidence in technology valuations and AI-related capital spending.[4]

items.title: Alstom cuts guidance after technical and production problems
items.summary: Alstom shares plunged after the French train maker reduced guidance, citing technical and production issues affecting products including its Coradia Max regional trains.[4]

items.title: Check Point revenue misses expectations
items.summary: Check Point Software reported non-GAAP earnings of $2.49 per share, in line with expectations, while revenue of $669.8 million missed the consensus estimate by about $2.34 million.[5]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Crypto market rebounds as Bitcoin nears $79,000
items.summary: Bitcoin rose about 1% over 24 hours to roughly $78,600, while Ethereum and BNB gained nearly 2% and Zcash advanced about 3%. The broader market recovered toward a $2.62 trillion capitalization, although Bitcoin remained affected by October’s 7.5% decline and weak ETF flows.

items.title: Binance restores withdrawals after $6.3 billion hack
items.summary: Binance resumed withdrawals across 15 blockchain networks after a reported North Korea-linked hack drained approximately $6.3 billion from hot wallets. The exchange also completed a transfer of 7,499 BTC, worth about $581 million, from its SAFU insurance fund.

items.title: Binance completes 7,499 BTC SAFU transfer
items.summary: Binance confirmed that it transferred 7,499 BTC from its Secure Asset Fund for Users, following on-chain monitoring that identified the transaction. The transfer was valued at approximately $581 million.

items.title: USDC Treasury mints $250 million on Solana
items.summary: The USDC Treasury minted 250 million USDC on the Solana blockchain, according to on-chain monitoring data. The issuance adds roughly $250 million in dollar-backed liquidity to the network.

items.title: SOON suspends svmBNB bridge after abnormal withdrawals
items.summary: The SOON Foundation temporarily shut its cross-chain bridge between svmBNB and the SOON mainnet after detecting abnormal withdrawals on October 31. The bridge is under control while an investigation continues.

items.title: US crypto legislation faces renewed attention after Binance hack
items.summary: Senator Cynthia Lummis and the Digital Chamber renewed calls for legislation addressing crypto security and market oversight after the Binance incident. Debate over the CLARITY Act remains significant because it would clarify regulatory responsibilities between U.S. agencies.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic introduces Claude Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5
items.summary: Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5.5, describing it as optimized for agentic coding and knowledge work at lower operating cost than Opus 5. The company also introduced Claude Haiku 5.5 for high-volume tasks such as summarization, subagents, and browser use.

items.title: Baidu open-sources Unlimited OCR 2
items.summary: Baidu released a document-parsing model designed to process very large files without linearly increasing decoding costs. Its sparse-reference attention architecture focuses each decoding step on selected visual references.

items.title: Liquid AI releases open-weight LFM3 model family
items.summary: Liquid AI released six compact open-weight models built on a shared foundation, covering text, vision, speech, multimodal assistance, and structured decision-making. The models target local deployment and fine-tuning.

items.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe
items.summary: NVIDIA introduced an open-weight speech model supporting transcription in 40 languages, translation, speaker attribution, formatting control, and audio question answering through natural-language instructions.

items.title: Hugging Face Bio releases FineDNA training data
items.summary: Hugging Face Bio released training data and recipe information for Carbon-X’s DNA-focused model, giving researchers more visibility into its data mixture and development process.

items.title: Meta releases official implementation of WaiT image-generation research
items.summary: Meta published code for WaiT, a wavelet-aware image Transformer intended to improve generation efficiency through frequency-aware flow matching. The implementation supports class-conditional ImageNet generation.

items.title: Google reports AI model execution on an orbital TPU
items.summary: Google said its Project Suncatcher prototype successfully ran the Gemma 4 model on a data-center-class Tensor Processing Unit in orbit and transmitted a generated response to Earth.

items.title: Google DeepMind expands AI planning tool across UK councils
items.summary: Google DeepMind is expanding its Gemini-powered PlanAssist tool into a 12-month beta across 15 English councils. The system aggregates application documents, policies, and constraints into cited draft assessments for routine planning cases.

items.title: AI firms back common robots.txt training restriction standard
items.summary: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic reportedly agreed to support a proposed standard allowing website owners to specify AI-training restrictions through robots.txt. Anthropic has begun supporting it, with other companies expected to follow.

items.title: Cisco Talos identifies AI-assisted information-stealing malware
items.summary: Cisco Talos researchers identified VOLTA, malware that can use commercial AI models to analyze stolen credentials and personal information and rank them by potential value. The AI component is optional and can switch models when one refuses a request.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero sells 4 million copies in 72 hours
items.summary: S-Game’s action RPG Phantom Blade Zero sold more than 4 million copies across PC and PlayStation 5 within its first 72 hours, marking a major commercial success for the Chinese developer.

items.title: Phantom Blade Zero exceeds 700,000 concurrent Steam players
items.summary: Phantom Blade Zero reportedly peaked above 700,000 concurrent players on Steam during its first 24 hours, placing it among the platform’s biggest launches.

items.title: The Duskbloods delayed to 2027
items.summary: FromSoftware has delayed The Duskbloods from its planned 2026 window to 2027, reducing the Nintendo Switch 2’s expected third-party lineup for this year.

items.title: Penguin Colony aims to challenge the games industry
items.summary: Origanme Digital discussed Penguin Colony, a psychological-horror game inspired by H.P. Lovecraft and told through the perspective of Antarctica’s Indigenous inhabitants.

items.title: Modern Warfare 4 Season 1 launches November 6
items.summary: PlayStation detailed the content and launch plans for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Season 1, scheduled to begin November 6.

items.title: Netflix gaming executive joins Xbox
items.summary: Christopher Lee, previously Netflix’s gaming content lead, has moved to Xbox as general manager of portfolio planning and partner marketing.

items.title: Scopely invests in studio formed by former Glu developers
items.summary: Veterans behind Covet Fashion and Design Home have established Burlingame, which received a $20 million investment from Scopely.

items.title: Activision confirms Warzone Mobile follow-up through hiring push
items.summary: Activision has confirmed development of a new Call of Duty: Warzone mobile project while seeking additional talent for the title.
